chunks: My father and the group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Aban, from al-Sadusi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever comes to me as a visitor (Zā'ir), I will be his intercessor on the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.a.w.) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith establishes the profound spiritual merit of visiting the Prophet’s grave, linking physical devotion to eschatological intercession. It underscores the Shia belief that such visitation is not merely a ritual but a means of securing the Prophet’s personal advocacy (Shafa'ah) on the Day of Judgment, reflecting the enduring bond between the believer and the Messenger.
